ordered_candidate_plan.angle: Positive Tesla free cash flow came alongside capital spending below expectations, even though spending remained more than double the prior-year level. Explain why this surprise needs a spending-versus-operating-cash distinction before it can be read as durable profitability.
ordered_candidate_plan.evidence_plan: Use only retained goal35-tesla Reuters facts, published 2026-10-21T20:06:00Z and known at 2026-10-21T22:27:23.026Z. Bind September-quarter free cash flow $1.53 billion against expected cash burn $4.92 billion; Q3 capital expenditure $4.73 billion against roughly $7.5 billion analyst estimate. Preserve the separately rounded $4.7 billion statement and reported more-than-double year-ago comparison; do not treat lower than expected as a year-on-year spending cut. Reuters headline frames the AI-spending connection; the retained numbers are total capex, not an independently measured AI-only spending breakdown. Attribute all facts and estimates to Reuters/LSEG as supplied. Explain qualitatively that cash remaining after capital spending can improve when less cash is invested than expected; do not assert deferral, cancellation, efficiency, or timing is established. Missing: operating-cash-flow bridge, working-capital drivers, exact capex timing/composition, future commitments and repeatability. No inferred earnings improvement, demand acceleration or investment returns. Code owns arithmetic; no hand-calculated surprise bridge or residual attribution. No new sources, requests, quotations or media.
ordered_candidate_plan.primary_reader_question: How much does positive Tesla free cash flow tell investors when capital spending was below expectations but still more than double a year earlier?
research_queries: Tesla October 21 2026 free cash flow capital expenditure expectations AI spending
ordered_candidate_plan.selection_rationale: A fresh cash-flow surprise supports a useful current question about the quality and persistence of cash generation. It is distinct from IBM software-demand composition, handled oil and historical company-reading research. The spending comparison prevents a misleading cost-cutting interpretation while preserving the real reported positive cash outcome. Single-source report truth only.

output.selection_summary: Select Tesla only. Explain the cash-flow surprise alongside lower-than-expected but sharply higher year-on-year capex, without equating free cash flow with profit or proving the spending difference was deferred.
